key_insight: ArogyaSutra combines multimodal tool-grounded reasoning with an actor-critic multi-agent design to improve medical question answering in English and seven Indic languages.
engineering_relevance: The work offers a practical blueprint for building clinically useful multilingual MLLMs that can better serve low-resource, image-supported healthcare settings.
method: ArogyaBodha: a large multilingual multimodal medical QA dataset from 8 sources, spanning 31 body systems, 6 imaging modalities, and 21 clinical domains.
ArogyaSutra: an actor-critic-based multi-agent framework with tool grounding for step-wise medical reasoning.
Dual-memory and stored simulation trajectories are used to support reasoning and distillation.
evidence_signal: Experiments on the new dataset show improved multilingual medical reasoning accuracy across all Indic languages, with ablation studies confirming the value of each component.
watch_item: Clinical deployment will need careful validation for hallucinations, safety, and reliability across diverse languages, modalities, and patient populations.
paper_title: ArogyaSutra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Multimodal Medical Reasoning in Indic Languages
